questions.explanation: Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) requires that children with disabilities be educated with children who are non-disabled to the maximum extent appropriate, resorting to special classes only when severity demands.

questions.question: Under the Indian Government's SWAYAM portal for Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), what are the four designated structural quadrants of learning delivery?
options: e-Tutorial (video), e-Content (reading), Self-Assessment (tests), and Online Discussion Forum
Live Broadcast, Radio Lessons, Physical Textbooks, and Lab Manuals
Primary, Upper Primary, Secondary, and Higher Secondary content
Registration, Attendance, Term Examinations, and Certification
questions.explanation: SWAYAM courses are structured into 4 quadrants: Quadrant I (e-Tutorial - Video/Audio), Quadrant II (e-Content - Reading material/e-Books), Quadrant III (Self-Assessment - Tests/Quizzes), and Quadrant IV (Discussion Forum - Doubts).

questions.question: In the TPACK framework developed by Mishra and Koehler for effective technology integration in instruction, what does 'TPACK' stand for?
options: Technical, Pedagogical, and Applied Content Knowledge
Teaching, Planning, Assessment, and Communication Knowledge
Technological Process and Administrative Curriculum Knowledge
questions.explanation: TPACK stands for Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge, describing the complex interaction between technology, pedagogy, and content knowledge required for effective tech-based teaching.

questions.question: Which systematic 10-step instructional design framework relies heavily on a systems approach involving instructional goals, performance objectives, criterion-referenced test items, and formative/summative evaluations?
questions.explanation: The Dick and Carey Model (Systems Approach Model) is a well-known 10-step instructional design framework that views instruction as a systematic process with interconnected components.

questions.question: In Ralph Tyler's classical model of curriculum construction ('Tyler Rationale'), what is the correct logical starting point for curriculum design?
options: Defining educational goals and learning objectives
questions.explanation: Ralph Tyler's four fundamental questions begin with defining clear educational objectives, followed by selecting learning experiences, organizing experiences, and evaluating outcomes.

questions.question: Who introduced the concept of the 'Spiral Curriculum', which asserts that any subject can be taught effectively in some intellectually honest form to any child at any stage of development?
questions.explanation: Jerome Bruner introduced the 'Spiral Curriculum' in his 1960 book 'The Process of Education', proposing that foundational concepts should be revisited at progressively higher levels of complexity.

questions.question: Carl Rogers established Person-Centred (Non-Directive) Therapy. Which of the following is NOT one of Rogers' three necessary and sufficient core conditions for therapeutic change?
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers identified three core conditions: Congruence (genuineness), Unconditional Positive Regard (acceptance), and Empathic Understanding. Directive/diagnostic interpretation is explicitly avoided in non-directive counselling.

questions.question: What is the standard time duration allocated for the 'Teach' phase in the Indian model of Microteaching developed by NCERT?
questions.explanation: In the NCERT model of Microteaching, the standard cycle consists of 36 minutes total: Teaching (6 min), Feedback (6 min), Re-plan (12 min), Re-teach (6 min), and Re-feedback (6 min). Thus, the 'Teach' phase is allocated 6 minutes.

or.question: NCERT ଦ୍ୱାରା ବିକଶିତ ଭାରତୀୟ ମାଇକ୍ରୋଟିଚିଂ (ସୂକ୍ଷ୍ମ ଶିକ୍ଷଣ) ମଡେଲରେ 'ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ' (Teach) ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ପାଇଁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଧାରିତ ମାନକ ସମୟସୀମା କେତେ?
or.explanation: NCERT ର ସୂକ୍ଷ୍ମ ଶିକ୍ଷଣ ମଡେଲରେ ସମୁଦାୟ ଚକ୍ର ୩୬ ମିନିଟର ଅଟେ: ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ (୬ ମିନିଟ୍), ଫିଡବ୍ୟାକ୍ (୬ ମିନିଟ୍), ପୁନଃ-ଯୋଜନା (୧୨ ମିନିଟ୍), ପୁନଃ-ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ (୬ ମିନିଟ୍), ଏବଂ ପୁନଃ-ଫିଡବ୍ୟାକ୍ (୬ ମିନିଟ୍)। ତେଣୁ, 'ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ' ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ପାଇଁ ୬ ମିନିଟ୍ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଧାରିତ।

questions.question: According to Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development, at which sub-stage of the Sensorimotor stage does a child first demonstrate 'A-not-B error' behavior?
options: Sub-stage 4: Coordination of Secondary Circular Reactions
questions.explanation: The 'A-not-B error' (or perseverative error) typically occurs in Sub-stage 4 (Coordination of Secondary Circular Reactions, around 8–12 months), where an infant searches for a hidden object in location A (where it was previously found) even after watching it being moved to location B.

or.question: ଜାଁ ପିଆଜେଙ୍କ ଜ୍ଞାନାତ୍ମକ ବିକାଶ ସିଦ୍ଧାନ୍ତ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ, ସେନ୍ସୋରୀମୋଟର (ସଂବେଦୀ-ପ୍ରେରକ) ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟର କେଉଁ ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟରେ ଶିଶୁ ପ୍ରଥମେ 'A-not-B ତ୍ରୁଟି' (A-not-B error) ଆଚରଣ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ କରେ?
options: ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ୨: ପ୍ରାଥମିକ ବୃତ୍ତାକାର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା (Primary Circular Reactions)
ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ୩: ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟକ ବୃତ୍ତାକାର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା (Secondary Circular Reactions)
ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ୪: ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟକ ବୃତ୍ତାକାର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ସମନ୍ୱୟ (Coordination of Secondary Circular Reactions)
ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ୫: ତୃତୀୟକ ବୃତ୍ତାକାର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା (Tertiary Circular Reactions)
or.explanation: 'A-not-B ତ୍ରୁଟି' ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଉପ-ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ୪ (ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟକ ବୃତ୍ତାକାର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ସମନ୍ୱୟ, ପ୍ରାୟ ୮-୧୨ ମାସ) ରେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ଯେଉଁଠାରେ ଶିଶୁଟି ଏକ ଲୁଚାଯାଇଥିବା ବସ୍ତୁକୁ 'स्थान B' କୁ ସ୍ଥାନାନ୍ତର କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଦେଖିବା ପରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା 'स्थान A' ରେ ହିଁ ଖୋଜିଥାଏ।

questions.question: Which branch of psychology focuses specifically on the scientific study of human learning processes, pedagogical interventions, and psychological aspects of educational settings?
questions.explanation: Educational Psychology is the branch of psychology concerned with how human beings learn in educational settings, evaluating instructional techniques, and understanding individual differences in learning.

questions.question: According to developmental psychology, the 'Cephalocaudal' trend of physical development dictates that motor control and growth proceed from:
options: The center of the body outward to extremities
General motor responses to specific responses
questions.explanation: The cephalocaudal principle states that development proceeds from top to bottom; a child gains control over head and facial movements before legs and feet.

questions.question: Which developmental principle states that physical growth and development proceed outward from the central longitudinal axis of the body toward the extremities?
questions.explanation: The proximodistal principle of development asserts that growth proceeds from the center of the body outward (e.g., control over arms before fingers).

questions.question: In Jean Piaget's theory, when a child understands that the quantity of a liquid remains the same despite being poured into a tall, narrow glass from a short, wide beaker, the child has developed:
questions.explanation: Conservation is the realization that fundamental physical properties (mass, volume, quantity) remain constant even when outward appearance changes, achieved in the Concrete Operational stage.

questions.question: According to Piaget's preoperational stage analysis, a young child's belief that non-living physical objects (such as the Sun or a doll) possess intentions, emotions, and life-like qualities is known as:
questions.explanation: Animism is the tendency of preoperational children to attribute human feelings, intentions, and consciousness to inanimate objects.

questions.question: In Lev Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory, what does the acronym 'ZPD' stand for?
questions.explanation: ZPD stands for the Zone of Proximal Development, defined as the distance between actual independent problem-solving ability and potential development under guidance.

questions.question: In Vygotskyian pedagogy, temporary instructional support given by a teacher or more competent peer, which is gradually removed as the student gains autonomy, is termed:
questions.explanation: Scaffolding (a term popularized by Jerome Bruner in connection with Vygotsky's work) refers to tailored support provided to learners within their ZPD.

questions.question: According to Lawrence Kohlberg's theory, an individual who obeys rules purely to avoid physical punishment is operating at which level of moral development?
questions.explanation: Stage 1 (Punishment and Obedience Orientation) falls under the Pre-conventional level, where moral decisions are determined by direct physical consequences.

questions.question: In Lawrence Kohlberg's stage model, Stage 5 (Social Contract and Individual Rights) belongs to which broader level of moral reasoning?
questions.explanation: Stage 5 (Social Contract and Individual Rights) and Stage 6 (Universal Ethical Principles) comprise Level III: Post-conventional Morality.

questions.question: In Ivan Pavlov's classical conditioning experiments, before any conditioning took place, the sound of the bell initially served as a/an:
questions.explanation: Before association with meat powder, the sound of the bell elicited no salivation response and acted strictly as a Neutral Stimulus (NS).

questions.question: In B.F. Skinner's Operant Conditioning framework, removing an unpleasant stimulus (such as exempting a student from a hated chore) after a desired behavior occurs is an application of:
questions.explanation: Negative Reinforcement involves strengthening a behavior by removing or suppressing an aversive or unpleasant stimulus.

questions.question: In Atkinson and Shiffrin's stage model of memory, which memory structure has an virtually unlimited capacity and can retain information over extended periods?
questions.explanation: Long-Term Memory (LTM) is considered to have unlimited capacity and long duration, storing information across days, years, or a lifetime.

questions.question: In Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory, which type of cognitive load refers specifically to the inherent complexity and internal structure of the instructional material itself?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic Cognitive Load is generated by the inherent difficulty and element interactivity of the material to be learned, independent of instructional design.

questions.question: Which fundamental principle best defines Ernst von Glasersfeld's perspective of Radical Constructivism?
options: Knowledge is passively received from external reality through direct observation
Knowledge is actively built up by the cognizing subject, not passively received from the environment
Learning is driven exclusively by observable stimulus-response contingencies
Cognitive development is entirely predetermined by genetic maturation
questions.explanation: Radical Constructivism, formulated by von Glasersfeld, posits that knowledge is actively constructed by the learner rather than passively absorbed from an objective reality.

questions.question: In the widely adopted 5E Constructivist Instructional Model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate), which phase explicitly aims to uncover prior knowledge and activate curiosity?
questions.explanation: The 'Engage' phase is the first step of the 5E Model, designed to spark student interest, capture attention, and reveal existing prior conceptions.

questions.question: In Ned Flanders' Interaction Analysis Categories System (FIACS), how many total categories are dedicated specifically to 'Teacher Talk'?
questions.explanation: FIACS consists of a total of 10 categories: 7 categories for Teacher Talk (4 for Indirect Influence and 3 for Direct Influence), 2 categories for Student Talk, and 1 category for Silence or Confusion.

or.question: ନେଡ୍ ଫ୍ଲାଣ୍ଡର୍ସଙ୍କ 'ଇଣ୍ଟରାକ୍ସନ୍ ଆନାଲିସିସ୍ କାଟେଗୋରୀ ସିଷ୍ଟମ୍' (FIACS) ରେ, 'ଶିକ୍ଷକଙ୍କ କଥା' (Teacher Talk) ପାଇଁ ସମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ବର୍ଗ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କରାଯାଇଛି?
or.explanation: FIACS ରେ ମୋଟ ୧୦ ଟି ବର୍ଗ ରହିଛି: ଶିକ୍ଷକଙ୍କ କଥା ପାଇଁ ୭ ଟି ବର୍ଗ (ଅପ୍ରତ୍ୟକ୍ଷ ପ୍ରଭାବ ପାଇଁ ୪ ଟି ଏବଂ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟକ୍ଷ ପ୍ରଭାବ ପାଇଁ ୩ ଟି), ଛାତ୍ରଙ୍କ କଥା ପାଇଁ ୨ ଟି ବର୍ଗ ଏବଂ ନୀରବତା କିମ୍ବା ଦ୍ବନ୍ଦ୍ବ ପାଇଁ ୧ ଟି ବର୍ଗ।

questions.question: According to Robert Gagné's Nine Events of Instruction, which instructional event directly follows 'Presenting the Content'?
questions.explanation: Gagné's Nine Events of Instruction follow a specific sequence: 1. Gain attention, 2. Inform learners of objectives, 3. Stimulate recall of prior learning, 4. Present the content, 5. Provide learning guidance, 6. Elicit performance, 7. Provide feedback, 8. Assess performance, 9. Enhance retention and transfer. Therefore, providing learning guidance (Event 5) directly follows presenting the content (Event 4).

or.question: ରବର୍ଟ ଗାଗ୍ନେ (Robert Gagné) ଙ୍କ 'ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନର ନଅଟି ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ' (Nine Events of Instruction) ଅନୁସାରେ, 'ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ କରିବା' (Presenting the Content) ପରେ କେଉଁ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟଟି ସିଧାସଳଖ ଆସିଥାଏ?
options: ଶିକ୍ଷଣ ମାର୍ଗଦର୍ଶନ ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିବା (Providing Learning Guidance)
ପୂର୍ବ ଶିକ୍ଷଣର ସ୍ମରଣକୁ ଉଦ୍ଦୀପିତ କରିବା (Stimulating Recall of Prior Learning)
or.explanation: ଗାଗ୍ନେଙ୍କ ନଅଟି ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟର କ୍ରମ ହେଉଛି: ୧. ଧ୍ୟାନ ଆକର୍ଷଣ କରିବା, ୨. ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ବିଷୟରେ ଜଣାଇବା, ୩. ପୂର୍ବ ଶିକ୍ଷଣକୁ ସ୍ମରଣ କରାଇବା, ୪. ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ କରିବା, ୫. ଶିକ୍ଷଣ ମାର୍ଗଦର୍ଶନ ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିବା, ୬. କାର୍ଯ୍ୟଦକ୍ଷତା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରାଇବା, ୭. ପ୍ରତିପୋଷଣ ଯୋଗାଇବା, ୮. କାର୍ଯ୍ୟଦକ୍ଷତାର ମୂଲ୍ୟାଙ୍କନ କରିବା, ୯. ଧାରଣ ଏବଂ ସ୍ଥାନାନ୍ତର ବୃଦ୍ଧି କରିବା। ତେଣୁ ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ପରେ ଶିକ୍ଷଣ ମାର୍ଗଦର୍ଶନ ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିବା ଆସିଥାଏ।

questions.question: Which of the following plays by William Shakespeare is known as his shortest tragedy?
questions.explanation: Among William Shakespeare's major tragedies, 'Macbeth' is the shortest, consisting of only about 2,477 lines and approximately 17,000 words.

or.question: ୱିଲିୟମ୍ ଶେକ୍ସପିୟରଙ୍କ ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ନାଟକଗୁଡ଼ିକ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ତାଙ୍କର ସବୁଠାରୁ କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରତମ ଟ୍ରାଜେଡି ଭାବରେ ଜଣାଶୁଣା?
or.explanation: ୱିଲିୟମ୍ ଶେକ୍ସପିୟରଙ୍କ ପ୍ରମୁଖ ଟ୍ରାଜେଡିଗୁଡ଼ିକ ମଧ୍ୟରେ 'ମ୍ୟାକବେଥ୍' ସବୁଠାରୁ କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରତମ ଅଟେ, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ ପ୍ରାୟ ୨,୪୭୭ ଟି ଧାଡ଼ି ଏବଂ ପାଖାପାଖି ୧୭,୦୦୦ ଶବ୍ଦ ରହିଛି।

questions.question: Which of the following carbocations is the most stable due to complete octet resonance stabilization?
questions.explanation: In the methoxy methyl cation (CH3-O-CH2+), the unshared electron pair on the oxygen atom forms a pi bond with the adjacent positive carbon atom (CH3-O+=CH2). In this resonance contributor, every atom possesses a complete octet of valence electrons, making it exceptionally stable compared to carbocations stabilized only by hyperconjugation or simple aromatic resonance.

or.question: ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଷ୍ଟକ ରେଜୋନାନ୍ସ ସ୍ଥିରତା (complete octet resonance stabilization) ଯୋଗୁଁ ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁ କାର୍ବୋକାଟାୟନ୍ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ସ୍ଥିର?
or.explanation: ମେଥୋକ୍ସି ମେଥାଇଲ୍ କାର୍ବୋକାଟାୟନ୍ (CH3-O-CH2+) ରେ, ଅକ୍ସିଜେନ୍ ପରମାଣୁର ଏକକ ଇଲେକ୍ଟ୍ରନ୍ ଯୁଗ୍ମ ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ଧନାତ୍ମକ ଚାର୍ଜିତ କାର୍ବନ ସହିତ ଏକ ପାଇ (pi) ବନ୍ଧନ ଗଠନ କରେ (CH3-O+=CH2)। ଏହି ରେଜୋନାନ୍ସ ସଂରଚନାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ପରମାଣୁର ଅଷ୍ଟକ ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ହୋଇଥାଏ, ଯାହା ଏହାକୁ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସ୍ଥିର କରିଥାଏ।

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the languages Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 added four new languages—Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali—to the Eighth Schedule, raising the total number of officially recognized languages in India to 22.

or.question: ଭାରତୀୟ ସମ୍ବିଧାନର କେଉଁ ସଂଶୋଧନ ଆଇନ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଅଷ୍ଟମ ଅନୁସୂଚୀରେ ବୋଡୋ, ଡୋଗ୍ରୀ, ମୈଥିଲୀ ଏବଂ ସନ୍ତାଳୀ ଭାଷା ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଥିଲା?
or.explanation: ୨୦୦୩ ମସିହାର ୯୨ତମ ସମ୍ବିଧାନ ସଂଶୋଧନ ଆଇନ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଭାରତୀୟ ସମ୍ବିଧାନର ଅଷ୍ଟମ ଅନୁସୂଚୀରେ ବୋଡୋ, ଡୋଗ୍ରୀ, ମୈଥିଲୀ ଏବଂ ସନ୍ତାଳୀ ଭାଷା ସାମିଲ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା, ଯାହାଫଳରେ ସ୍ୱୀକୃତିପ୍ରାପ୍ତ ଭାଷା ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୨୨ କୁ ବୃଦ୍ଧି ପାଇଥିଲା।

questions.question: In the context of the Indian Freedom Struggle, who among the following founded the 'Indian Independence League' in Tokyo in March 1942?
questions.explanation: Rash Behari Bose founded the Indian Independence League during a conference held in Tokyo in March 1942 to organize Indians living outside India for the liberation of their homeland. He later handed over its leadership to Subhas Chandra Bose.

or.question: ଭାରତୀୟ ସ୍ୱାଧୀନତା ସଂଗ୍ରାମ ସନ୍ଦର୍ଭରେ, ୧୯୪୨ ମସିହା ମାର୍ଚ୍ଚ ମାସରେ ଟୋକିଓଠାରେ 'ଇଣ୍ଡିଆନ୍ ଇଣ୍ଡିପେଣ୍ଡେନ୍ସ ଲିଗ୍'ର ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠା ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କିଏ କରିଥିଲେ?
or.explanation: ୧୯୪୨ ମସିହା ମାର୍ଚ୍ଚ ମାସରେ ଟୋକିଓରେ ଅନୁଷ୍ଠିତ ଏକ ସମ୍ମିଳନୀରେ ରାସ ବିହାରୀ ବୋସ 'ଇଣ୍ଡିଆନ୍ ଇଣ୍ଡିପେଣ୍ଡେନ୍ସ ଲିଗ୍' ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠା କରିଥିଲେ। ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସମୟରେ, ସେ ଏହାର ନେତୃତ୍ୱ ସୁଭାଷ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ବୋସଙ୍କୁ ହସ୍ତାନ୍ତର କରିଥିଲେ।

questions.question: Which leadership style in classroom management involves giving complete freedom to students with minimal teacher intervention or direct instruction?
questions.explanation: The Laissez-faire leadership style allows students complete freedom to make decisions without direct guidance, structure, or intervention from the teacher.

questions.question: Which term was coined by educational theorist Jacob Kounin to describe a teacher's skill in communicating to students that they are aware of everything occurring in the classroom at all times?
questions.explanation: Jacob Kounin introduced 'Withitness' to describe a teacher's acute awareness of classroom activities and prompt addressing of misbehavior.

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of the four fundamental steps in the Action Research cycle?
questions.explanation: The standard Action Research cycle follows a continuous spiral process of Plan, Act, Observe, and Reflect.

questions.question: Which methodological feature is LEAST appropriate for a classroom-based Action Research project carried out by a school teacher?
options: Immediate application to local classroom problems
Complex multi-stage probability sampling for external generalization
Use of qualitative observational checklists and diagnostic tests
questions.explanation: Action Research aims at immediate local context problem-solving, not large-scale generalization that requires complex multi-stage probability sampling.

questions.question: Under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, what is the new pedagogical and curricular structure replacing the former 10+2 system?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 restructures school education into 5 years (Foundational) + 3 years (Preparatory) + 3 years (Middle) + 4 years (Secondary).

questions.question: Under NEP 2020, what does the acronym 'PARAKH' stand for in the context of student assessment?
options: Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development
Program for Academic Assessment, Review, and Knowledge Enhancement
Pedagogical Assessment, Rating, and Analysis of Knowledge for Higher Education
Performance Appraisal, Recognition, and Assessment of Knowledge for High-schools
questions.explanation: PARAKH stands for Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development, set up as a National Assessment Centre.

questions.question: According to the Schedule of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, what is the prescribed Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for primary schools (Classes I to V) with enrollment up to 200 children?
questions.explanation: The RTE Act 2009 prescribes a Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) of 30:1 for primary schools for an enrollment up to 200 students.

questions.question: Which specific section of the Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009 explicitly prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment of children in schools?
questions.explanation: Section 17 of the RTE Act 2009 prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment of children and makes it a punishable offense.

questions.question: The National Curriculum Framework 2005 (NCF 2005) was prepared under the chairmanship of which eminent academician?
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 was drafted by the National Steering Committee under the leadership of renowned physicist and educationist Prof. Yash Pal.

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency represents the score that occurs with the highest frequency in a given distribution?
questions.explanation: The mode is defined as the most frequently occurring score in a set of data.

questions.question: In a standard normal distribution curve, approximately what percentage of the total observations falls within one standard deviation above and below the mean (±1 SD)?
questions.explanation: Under a normal curve, approximately 68.26% of the values fall within ±1 standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question: When a test score distribution is negatively skewed (skewed to the left), what is the correct relative magnitude relationship among Mean, Median, and Mode?
questions.explanation: In a negatively skewed distribution, extreme low scores pull the Mean to the left, making Mean < Median < Mode (or Mode > Median > Mean).

questions.question: Who proposed the Nativist theory of language acquisition featuring the concept of an innate Language Acquisition Device (LAD)?
questions.explanation: Noam Chomsky proposed that humans possess an innate capacity for language acquisition through a hypothetical Language Acquisition Device (LAD).

questions.question: In Stephen Krashen's theory of second language acquisition, which hypothesis argues that language learning occurs best when input is one step beyond the learner's current stage of competence (i + 1)?
questions.explanation: The Input Hypothesis states that language acquisition takes place when a learner receives 'comprehensible input' that is slightly above their current level (i + 1).

questions.question: What form of memory interference occurs when newly learned material interferes with the recall of previously stored information?
questions.explanation: Retroactive interference happens when new information acts backward to disrupt the retrieval of previously learned information.

questions.question: According to NCERT norms, what is the total duration allocated for one complete cycle of Microteaching in teacher training?
questions.explanation: As per the Indian (NCERT) model of microteaching, a full cycle takes 36 minutes, broken down as: Teaching (6 min), Feedback (6 min), Re-planning (12 min), Re-teaching (6 min), and Re-feedback (6 min).

or.question: NCERT ନିୟମ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ, ଶିକ୍ଷକ ପ୍ରଶିକ୍ଷଣରେ ମାଇକ୍ରୋଟିଚିଂ (Microteaching) ର ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଚକ୍ର ପାଇଁ ମୋଟ କେତେ ସମୟ ବରାଦ କରାଯାଇଛି?
or.explanation: ଭାରତୀୟ (NCERT) ମାଇକ୍ରୋଟିଚିଂ ମଡେଲ୍ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ, ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଚକ୍ରର ମୋଟ ଅବଧି ହେଉଛି 36 ମିନିଟ୍: ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ (6 ମିନିଟ୍), ପ୍ରତିପୁଷ୍ଟି (6 ମିନିଟ୍), ପୁନଃ-ଯୋଜନା (12 ମିନିଟ୍), ପୁନଃ-ଶିକ୍ଷାଦାନ (6 ମିନିଟ୍), ଏବଂ ପୁନଃ-ପ୍ରତିପୁଷ୍ଟି (6 ମିନିଟ୍)।

questions.question: In David Krathwohl's taxonomy of the Affective Domain, which level represents the highest hierarchical stage where an individual acts consistently in accordance with an internalized system of values?
options: Characterization by Value or Value Complex
questions.explanation: Krathwohl's Affective Domain consists of five levels in ascending order: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organization, and Characterization by Value or Value Complex. The highest level, Characterization, occurs when a person's behaviour is consistently guided by their internal value system.

or.question: ଡେଭିଡ୍ କ୍ରାଥୱୋଲଙ୍କ (David Krathwohl) ଭାବାତ୍ମକ କ୍ଷେତ୍ର (Affective Domain) ର ବର୍ଗୀକରଣରେ, କେଉଁ ସ୍ତରଟି ସର୍ବୋଚ୍ଚ ପଦାନୁକ୍ରମିକ ସ୍ତରକୁ ପ୍ରତିନିଧିତ୍ଵ କରେ ଯେଉଁଠାରେ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ନିଜର ଆଭ୍ୟନ୍ତରୀଣ ମୂଲ୍ୟବୋଧ ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ ନିରନ୍ତର କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କରେ?
options: ମୂଲ୍ୟବୋଧ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଚରିତ୍ରଗଠନ (Characterization by Value or Value Complex)
or.explanation: କ୍ରାଥୱୋଲଙ୍କ ଭାବାତ୍ମକ କ୍ଷେତ୍ରରେ ଆରୋହୀ କ୍ରମରେ ୫ଟି ସ୍ତର ରହିଛି: ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବା (Receiving), ଅନୁକ୍ରିୟା (Responding), ମୂଲ୍ୟାଙ୍କନ (Valuing), ସଂଗଠନ (Organization), ଏବଂ ମୂଲ୍ୟବୋଧ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଚରିତ୍ରଗଠନ (Characterization by Value) ଯାହା ସର୍ବୋଚ୍ଚ ସ୍ତର ଅଟେ।

questions.question: According to Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience, which of the following learning experiences provides the highest level of directness and retention?
questions.explanation: At the base of Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience lie 'Direct Purposeful Experiences'. These involve first-hand, concrete experiences where the learner uses all senses, leading to the highest degree of directness and knowledge retention.

or.question: ଏଡଗାର ଡେଲଙ୍କ 'କୋନ୍ ଅଫ୍ ଏକ୍ସପେରିଏନ୍ସ' (Cone of Experience) ଅନୁସାରେ, ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁ ଶିକ୍ଷଣ ଅନୁଭୂତି ସବୁଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟକ୍ଷତା ଏବଂ ମନେରଖିବା କ୍ଷମତା ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିଥାଏ?
or.explanation: ଏଡଗାର ଡେଲଙ୍କ ଅନୁଭବ କୋନ୍ (Cone of Experience) ର ସବୁଠାରୁ ତଳ ଭାଗରେ 'ପ୍ରତ୍ୟକ୍ଷ ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟମୂଳକ ଅନୁଭୂତି' ରହିଛି। ଏହା ଶିକ୍ଷାର୍ଥୀଙ୍କୁ ସବୁଠାରୁ ବାସ୍ତବ ଏବଂ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟକ୍ଷ ଅନୁଭୂତି ପ୍ରଦାନ କରେ, ଯାହାଦ୍ୱାରା ସର୍ବାଧିକ ଧାରଣ (retention) ସମ୍ଭବ ହୋଇଥାଏ।

questions.question: In J. P. Guilford's original (1967) Structure of Intellect (SOI) model, how many distinct mental abilities/factors were identified by combining Operations, Contents, and Products?
questions.explanation: In Guilford's original 1967 model, intelligence was conceptualized as a three-dimensional framework comprising 5 Operations, 4 Contents, and 6 Products. Multiplying these dimensions (5 × 4 × 6) yielded 120 unique factors/cells.

or.question: ଜେ. ପି. ଗିଲଫୋର୍ଡଙ୍କ ମୂଳ (୧୯୬୭) 'ବୁଦ୍ଧିମତ୍ତାର ସଂରଚନା' (Structure of Intellect - SOI) ମଡେଲରେ, ପ୍ରକ୍ରିୟା (Operations), ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ (Contents) ଏବଂ ଉତ୍ପାଦ (Products) ର ମିଶ୍ରଣ ଦ୍ୱାରା କେତୋଟି ମୋଟ ମାନସିକ କ୍ଷମତା/କାରକ ଚିହ୍ନଟ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା?
or.explanation: ଗିଲଫୋର୍ଡଙ୍କ ୧୯୬୭ ର ମୂଳ SOI ମଡେଲରେ ୫ ଟି ପ୍ରକ୍ରିୟା (Operations), ୪ ଟି ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ (Contents) ଏବଂ ୬ ଟି ଉତ୍ପାଦ (Products) ଥିଲା, ଯାହା ମୋଟ ୫ × ୪ × ୬ = ୧୨୦ ଟି କାରକ/କୋଠରୀ ଗଠନ କରୁଥିଲା।

questions.question: Which educational scheme, formulated by Mahatma Gandhi at the Wardha Conference in 1937, emphasized craft-centric and mother-tongue-based education?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi introduced the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education, popularised as 'Nai Talim', in 1937. It advocated craft-centered, free, and compulsory education taught in the child's mother tongue.

questions.question: In which year did Rabindranath Tagore formally establish the experimental school 'Brahmacharyasrama' (later known as Patha Bhavana) at Santiniketan?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore established his experimental school at Santiniketan on December 22, 1901, with five students. It later developed into Patha Bhavana under Visva-Bharati.

questions.question: Which German educator is universally recognized as the founder of the 'Kindergarten' system of early childhood education?
questions.explanation: Friedrich Froebel created the 'Kindergarten' (Garden of Children) system in Germany in 1837, emphasizing play, self-activity, and social interaction.

questions.question: According to John Dewey's pragmatic philosophy, how is 'education' formally defined in his seminal work 'Democracy and Education'?
options: The gradual acquisition of universal truths and permanent values
The continuous reconstruction or reorganization of experience
The preparation of the individual for ultimate spiritual salvation
The systematic conditioning of responses to environmental stimuli
questions.explanation: John Dewey famously defined education as 'that reconstruction or reorganization of experience which adds to the meaning of experience, and which increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience.'

questions.question: In Maria Montessori's framework of human development, which age period constitutes the 'Second Plane of Development', characterized by the emergence of the 'Reasoning Mind' and moral consciousness?
questions.explanation: Montessori identified four distinct planes of development: First Plane (0–6 years: Absorbent Mind), Second Plane (6–12 years: Reasoning Mind), Third Plane (12–18 years: Humanistic Mind), and Fourth Plane (18–24 years: Specialized Mind).

questions.question: Which specific neurodevelopmental learning disability primarily impairs a student's ability to understand, process, and perform mathematical calculations?
questions.explanation: Dyscalculia is a specific learning disorder that affects a person's ability to understand number concepts, learn arithmetic rules, and perform mathematical calculations.

questions.question: A student who consistently struggles with fine motor skills required for handwriting, letter spacing, line orientation, and spatial organisation on paper is diagnosed with:
questions.explanation: Dysgraphia is a neurological condition affecting written expression, fine motor coordination, spatial line management, and spelling ability.

questions.question: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 in India, what minimum degree of disability is required to classify an individual as having a 'benchmark disability'?
questions.explanation: Section 2(r) of the RPwD Act, 2016 defines a person with 'benchmark disability' as an individual with not less than 40% of a specified disability.

questions.question: In co-teaching instructional models for inclusive classrooms, which model involves both general and special educators presenting the exact same lesson simultaneously as equal leaders to the whole class?
questions.explanation: In Team Teaching (or Teaming), two teachers share equal responsibility for planning, instructing, and assessing the entire class together without dividing the room or students.

questions.question: In the Revised Bloom's Taxonomy of Cognitive Domain (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), which level represents the highest order of cognitive process?
questions.explanation: In Anderson and Krathwohl's 2001 revision of Bloom's Taxonomy, 'Creating' replaced 'Evaluation' at the top of the cognitive hierarchy.

questions.question: In the 4-Quadrant approach designed for SWAYAM MOOC courses by the Ministry of Education, India, which quadrant specifically provides 'Self-Assessment' tools like quizzes and tests?
questions.explanation: The 4 Quadrants of SWAYAM are: Quadrant I (E-Tutorial/Video), Quadrant II (E-Content/Reading), Quadrant III (Self-Assessment/Tests & Quizzes), and Quadrant IV (Discussion Forum).

questions.question: What is the primary technical objective of SCORM (Shareable Content Object Reference Model) in e-learning content administration?
options: Ensuring interoperability and reusability of learning content across different Learning Management Systems (LMS)
Automatically translating text-based lessons into localized spoken audio
questions.explanation: SCORM is a standard set of technical specifications for e-learning content that ensures learning materials are interoperable, reusable, and transferable across any SCORM-compliant Learning Management System (LMS).

questions.question: Which curriculum developer proposed an 'inductive' or 'grassroots' model, arguing that curriculum should be designed by teachers starting from specific learning units rather than top-down administrators?
questions.explanation: Hilda Taba advocated for an inductive (bottom-up/grassroots) approach to curriculum development, where teachers design learning units first before generalizing them into a broader curriculum.

questions.question: Who introduced the foundational conceptual distinction between 'Formative' and 'Summative' evaluation in curriculum and program evaluation in 1967?
questions.explanation: Michael Scriven introduced the concepts and terms 'formative evaluation' and 'summative evaluation' in his 1967 paper 'The Methodology of Evaluation'.

questions.question: Carl Rogers is widely recognized as the pioneer of which major approach to guidance and counseling?
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers pioneered Person-Centered (Non-Directive) Counseling, emphasizing unconditional positive regard, congruence, and counselor empathy to allow the client to lead self-discovery.

questions.question: Under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, what is the new pedagogical and curricular structure that replaces the earlier 10+2 system?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 replaces the 10+2 structure with a new 5+3+3+4 structure corresponding to ages 3-8 (Foundational), 8-11 (Preparatory), 11-14 (Middle), and 14-18 (Secondary).

questions.question: According to Section 3 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, children of which age group have the fundamental right to free and compulsory education?
questions.explanation: The RTE Act 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in a neighbourhood school until the completion of elementary education.

questions.question: Which component of the human memory system is characterized by an virtually unlimited storage capacity and the ability to retain information over long periods?
questions.explanation: Long-term memory (LTM) has an unlimited capacity and duration, allowing storage of information ranging from days to a lifetime.

questions.question: Who among the following social psychologists is widely recognized for coining the term 'Action Research' in the mid-1940s?
questions.explanation: Kurt Lewin coined the term 'Action Research' around 1944 to describe a process of cyclical inquiry to solve practical social problems.

questions.question: In Jacob Kounin's classroom management model, which term describes a teacher's ability to demonstrate total awareness of classroom activities and student behavior at all times?
questions.explanation: Kounin defined 'Withitness' as the teacher's ability to communicate to students that they know what is going on in all parts of the classroom at all times.

questions.question: According to Noam Chomsky, human children are born with an innate biological capacity that allows them to acquire language naturally. What is this construct called?
questions.explanation: Noam Chomsky proposed the concept of the Language Acquisition Device (LAD), an innate mental mechanism that enables children to construct the grammar of their native language.

questions.question: In a standard normal distribution curve, approximately what percentage of total cases lie within one standard deviation above and below the mean (±1σ)?
questions.explanation: In a normal distribution, approximately 68.26% (roughly 68%) of the area/cases fall within ±1 standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question: The National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE 2023) was developed under the leadership of the National Steering Committee headed by which eminent personality?
questions.explanation: Dr. K. Kasturirangan headed the National Steering Committee that drafted the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE 2023).

questions.question: Under the Schedule of the RTE Act 2009, what is the mandatory Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for primary classes (Classes I to V) for an enrolment up to 200 students?
questions.explanation: The RTE Act, 2009 specifies a Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) of 30:1 for primary schools (Classes I to V) up to an enrolment of 200 students.

questions.question: When newly learned information prevents or interferes with the retrieval of previously stored information, what phenomenon is occurring?
questions.explanation: Retroactive interference occurs when new learning disrupts the recall of older information, whereas proactive interference occurs when older memories disrupt new learning.

questions.question: According to Stephen M. Corey, who adapted action research to education, which sequence correctly reflects the essential steps of an action research cycle?
options: Identification of problem -> Formulation of action hypothesis -> Execution of plan & data collection -> Evaluation
Formulation of hypothesis -> Problem identification -> Action plan implementation -> Data collection
Execution of plan -> Problem identification -> Hypothesis formulation -> Data collection -> Evaluation
Collection of baseline data -> Problem identification -> Hypothesis formulation -> Implementation
questions.explanation: Corey's classic action research steps follow: identifying a practical problem, formulating an action hypothesis, executing the plan while collecting data, and evaluating the outcome.

questions.question: In educational testing, what is the constant value of the standard deviation for any set of standardized Z-scores?
questions.explanation: Z-scores convert raw scores into a standard distribution where the mean is always 0 and the standard deviation is always 1.

questions.question: In Stephen Krashen's Monitor Model, which hypothesis asserts that language acquisition occurs best when the learner receives language input that is one step beyond their current stage of competence?
questions.explanation: Krashen's Input Hypothesis proposes that learners acquire language when exposed to 'comprehensible input' represented as 'i+1', where 'i' is the learner's current competence and '+1' is the next step.

questions.question: In Rudolf Dreikurs' Model of Social Discipline, misbehavior in school children is driven by four 'mistaken goals'. Which of the following correctly lists all four mistaken goals?
options: Attention, Power, Revenge, Display of Inadequacy
questions.explanation: Dreikurs identified four mistaken goals of student misbehavior: seeking Attention, seeking Power, seeking Revenge, and Displaying Inadequacy (or assumed disability).

questions.question: In item analysis of a norm-referenced achievement test, an item has a Difficulty Index (P) of 0.85 and a Discrimination Index (D) of 0.05. What is the most appropriate psychometric decision?
options: Retain the item as it demonstrates excellent discrimination between groups.
Modify the distractors slightly to increase its overall difficulty.
Discard or thoroughly revise the item because its discrimination power is unacceptably low.
Increase the testing time allotted to students to balance item performance.
questions.explanation: A Discrimination Index below 0.20 indicates poor ability to differentiate high-performing from low-performing students. Combined with a very high difficulty index (0.85 = very easy), the item fails norm-referenced criteria and must be discarded or revised.

questions.question: Under Mahatma Gandhi's Wardha Scheme of Basic Education (Nai Talim, 1937), which committee was appointed to formulate the detailed national curriculum and syllabus?
questions.explanation: At the All India National Education Conference held at Wardha in October 1937, a committee under the chairmanship of Dr. Zakir Husain was appointed to formulate the detailed syllabus for Basic Education.

questions.question: In 1922, Rabindranath Tagore established the 'Institute of Rural Reconstruction' at Sriniketan with the collaboration and direct leadership of which British agricultural economist?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore founded Sriniketan (the Department of Rural Reconstruction) in February 1922 with the assistance of British agronomist Leonard Elmhirst, who served as its first director.

questions.question: In Friedrich Froebel's Kindergarten pedagogy, what did the 'First Gift' given to young children consist of?
options: A solid wooden sphere, cylinder, and cube
A wooden cube divided into eight smaller cubes
A set of colored wooden slats and sticks
questions.explanation: Froebel's First Gift consists of six soft, colored yarn balls (three primary colors: red, yellow, blue; and three secondary: green, orange, purple) designed to help infants perceive form, color, and motion.

questions.question: In the Montessori Method, Maria Montessori adapted the structured 'Three-Period Lesson' technique for language and sensorial teaching directly from the works of which pioneer educator?
questions.explanation: Maria Montessori heavily built upon the didactic methods of French physician Édouard Séguin, including his 'Three-Period Lesson' (Naming, Recognition, Pronunciation/Recall).

questions.question: According to John Dewey's seminal analysis of reflective thinking in 'How We Think' (1910), what is the initial phase/step that initiates reflective inquiry?
questions.explanation: Dewey identified five steps of reflective thinking, the first being a felt difficulty or state of perplexity/doubt, which prompts the learner to define the problem and seek solutions.

questions.question: Which specific developmental disorder is characterized primarily by difficulty with motor planning, physical coordination, and fine motor tasks such as handwriting, cutting, or buttoning?
questions.explanation: Dyspraxia (Developmental Coordination Disorder) affects motor skill development, motor planning, and body coordination, making fine and gross motor tasks challenging.

questions.question: In modern educational diagnostics, the tiered 'Response to Intervention' (RTI) framework was officially recognized as an alternative to the traditional 'Severe Discrepancy Model' for identifying Specific Learning Disabilities under which legislation?
options: IDEA 2004 (Individuals with Disabilities Education Improvement Act)
P.L. 94-142 (Education for All Handicapped Children Act of 1975)
No Child Left Behind Act of 2001
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973
questions.explanation: The reauthorization of IDEA in 2004 permitted states to eliminate the requirement for a severe discrepancy between IQ and achievement, allowing the use of Response to Intervention (RTI) for SLD identification.

questions.question: Under India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, how many benchmark categories of disabilities are legally recognized, compared to 7 in the previous 1995 Act?
questions.explanation: The RPwD Act 2016 expanded the list of recognized disabilities from 7 to 21, including conditions like Specific Learning Disabilities, Autism Spectrum Disorder, and Acid Attack Victimhood.

questions.question: In the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework developed by CAST, the three foundational principles (Engagement, Representation, Action & Expression) directly align with which three respective brain networks?
questions.explanation: UDL aligns multiple means of Engagement with the Affective network (the 'why'), Representation with the Recognition network (the 'what'), and Action & Expression with the Strategic network (the 'how').

questions.question: In Ruben Puentedura's SAMR model of educational technology integration, which two hierarchical levels constitute the 'Transformation' domain?
questions.explanation: In the SAMR model, Substitution and Augmentation belong to the 'Enhancement' domain, whereas Modification and Redefinition belong to the 'Transformation' domain.

questions.question: What is the full expansion of the acronym 'SWAYAM', the Government of India's indigenous MOOCs platform?
options: School-level Web Applications for Youth Academic Mastery
System of Web-based Assessment for Young Academic Minds
Student Welfare and Academic Yield Assessment Mechanism
Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
questions.explanation: SWAYAM stands for 'Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds', launched by the Ministry of Education to provide free online university and school courses.

questions.question: In the TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) model developed by Mishra and Koehler (2006), the integration of content knowledge and teaching strategies without technology represents which component originated by Lee Shulman?
questions.explanation: Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK) was originally conceptualized by Lee Shulman in 1986 to describe how teachers transform subject matter (CK) into teachable representations (PK).

questions.question: In Ralph Tyler's classic 1949 curriculum development rationale ('Basic Principles of Curriculum and Instruction'), which is the first fundamental question that must be resolved?
options: What educational purposes should the school seek to attain?
What educational experiences can be provided that are likely to attain these purposes?
How can these educational experiences be effectively organized?
How can we determine whether these purposes are being attained?
questions.explanation: Tyler's four-step rationale begins with identifying the educational goals/purposes the school seeks to achieve, followed by selecting experiences, organizing them, and evaluation.

questions.question: Hilda Taba proposed an inductive 'grassroots' model of curriculum development. What is the very first step in Taba's 7-step curriculum model?
questions.explanation: Unlike Tyler's top-down approach starting with objectives, Hilda Taba's inductive grassroots model begins with 'Diagnosis of learners' needs' carried out by classroom teachers.

questions.question: According to Carl Rogers' Person-Centered (Non-Directive) Counseling framework, which three 'core conditions' are both necessary and sufficient for constructive therapeutic change?
options: Direct Advice, Behavior Shaping, and Cognitive Restructuring
Congruence (Genuineness), Unconditional Positive Regard, and Empathic Understanding
Interpretation, Resistance Analysis, and Transference Resolution
Catharsis, Systematic Desensitization, and Aversive Conditioning
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers identified three core counselor-offered conditions: Congruence (realness/genuineness), Unconditional Positive Regard (acceptance), and accurate Empathic Understanding.
